quote: I enshrine the memory of pain inside a vessel, and let time turn it into hope.

paragraphs.heading: Where it began
paragraphs.text: In my early twenties, the installation “Fallen Leaves” at a Jewish museum in Germany opened my eyes to social violence and the pain of its victims. After painting, I found lacquer, and I have kept telling stories about violence through this natural material.

paragraphs.heading: To hold
paragraphs.text: A ham (函) is a vessel that keeps precious things, like a reliquary or a case for sutras. What I place in it is not an object but feelings and memories I could not put into words, and hope.

paragraphs.heading: Enshrinement
paragraphs.text: Enshrining is not forgetting or erasing a wound. It is keeping an unbearable memory at a bearable distance for a while, and opening it to look when the time comes.

paragraphs.heading: The seed
paragraphs.text: A seed sheds its husk and sprouts even in harsh conditions. I divided the life of a seed, from birth through growth, fruiting, fruit, aging and origin, among several vessels. I do not erase aging and cracks; I accept them as part of life.

paragraphs.heading: Dry lacquer and time
paragraphs.text: Dry lacquer (geonchil) builds up layers of hemp cloth, yellow ochre and lacquer, then hollows out the mold inside. Only what is emptied can hold something, and the long hours of drying, grinding and re-lacquering become a time of healing.

paragraphs.heading: To those who stand before it
paragraphs.text: I do not want the work to give only one interpretation. I hope you will set your own memories inside the vessel for a moment and take time to care for yourself.
